title: Cold launch — hero render
precondition: No SharedPreferences key age_verified; fresh install state

before_state.description: App not yet launched; blank simulator screen

after_state.description: WelcomeScreen fully rendered: AmbientBlob animated, BreathingIllustration pulsing, 3 TrustChips visible, Continue button present

judge_criteria: WelcomeScreen is visible (not blank or loading spinner)
At least one TrustChip pill visible (private/diagnosis/always-here)
No crash dialog or red error widget
persona_context: Maya just tapped the GentleQuest app for the very first time after seeing a TikTok. She's nervous and slightly embarrassed — she's never used a wellness app before. First impressions are everything.

title: Continue → age modal

before_state.description: WelcomeScreen hero fully rendered

after_state.description: AgeModal slides up as ModalBottomSheet; drag handle visible; both age buttons present

judge_criteria: 'Yes, I am 18 or older' ElevatedButton visible
Sheet is not dismissible (no dark scrim tap-away)
persona_context: Maya just tapped Continue. She's now being asked about her age — this is a gate. She wants to get in quickly; friction here could make her second-guess whether the app is worth it.

title: Age modal → 18+ confirmed → ComplianceGuard

before_state.description: AgeModal open with both age buttons

after_state.description: ComplianceGuardScreen renders; WelcomeScreen removed from stack

judge_criteria: 'I am 18 or older' button visible on new screen
persona_context: Maya confirmed she's 18+. She expects to land somewhere meaningful — the gate should feel lightweight, not like another barrier.

title: Age modal → under-18 dignity path

before_state.description: AgeModal open with both age buttons

after_state.description: Under18Screen renders with compassionate headline and resource cards

persona_context: An under-18 user just got redirected. This is not Maya, but this screen reflects the app's care for all users. Maya might show this to a younger friend — the dignity of this path matters.

title: Available region — standard age gate → HomeShell

before_state.description: ComplianceGuardScreen with both age buttons

after_state.description: HomeShell loads; bottom nav visible; Talk/Mood/Quest/Dashboard tabs present

judge_criteria: HomeShell is visible (bottom nav with tabs)
ComplianceGuardScreen is no longer on stack
Chat tab (Talk) or Mood tab visible
persona_context: Maya got through the gate. She's now in the app for the first time. Every second that takes before she sees something useful is trust draining.

title: First-turn render — Alex greeting visible
precondition: HomeShell loaded; Talk tab selected; no prior messages

before_state.description: HomeShell on another tab (Mood or Dashboard)

after_state.description: InteractiveChatScreen: Alex greeting bubble visible, suggestion chips present, TextField and Send button at bottom

judge_criteria: Alex greeting chat bubble visible (left-aligned, surface background)
Suggestion chips row visible ('Today's been heavy', 'I want to vent a little', 'Just need someone to listen', 'Quick win, please')
No blank chat area or loading spinner stuck
persona_context: Maya opened the Talk tab for the first time. She wants to feel welcomed and understood immediately — not face a blank screen or generic instructions.

title: Send a text message — full round-trip

before_state.description: Chat screen with empty TextField and Alex greeting bubble

after_state.description: User message bubble on right; typing indicator appeared then AI response bubble on left; TextField cleared

judge_criteria: User message bubble on right side of screen
No error dialog or red error bubble
At minimum typing indicator OR AI response bubble is visible
persona_context: Maya typed her first real feeling and hit send — she is waiting and vulnerable. If this fails, she will never open the app again.

title: Suggestion chip → prefill → send

before_state.description: Chat with suggestion chips visible ('Today's been heavy', 'I want to vent a little', etc.)

after_state.description: TextField prefilled with chip text; cursor at end; chips still present (not auto-sent)

judge_criteria: TextField shows text from the tapped chip
Message was NOT auto-sent (no user bubble in chat yet)
TextField cursor visible at end of prefilled text
persona_context: Maya saw 'Today's been heavy' and tapped it. She expected it to start her message for her — not send it. This micro-interaction either feels helpful or invasive.

title: Navigate to Profile via app bar icon
defining_action: Tap account_circle_outlined IconButton in app bar

before_state.description: Chat screen with app bar visible

after_state.description: ProfileNavSheet slides up as modal bottom sheet; navigation options 'Profile', 'Settings', 'Journal' visible

judge_criteria: At least 'Profile' or 'Settings' navigation option visible
Sheet overlays but does not cover the full screen
persona_context: Maya wants to check her profile. She tapped the avatar icon — she expects a quick path to her settings and personal info, not a navigation maze.

title: Mood tab render — no mood logged today
precondition: Mood tab selected; no mood logged today

before_state.description: HomeShell on Talk tab

after_state.description: MoodTrackerScreen with MoodTriggerCard (Check in CTA), ClinicalCheckInCard, WeeklyReviewRow all visible

judge_criteria: MoodTriggerCard visible with Check in CTA
persona_context: Maya opened the Mood tab for the first time today. She hasn't checked in yet. She wants a clear, low-friction path to log how she's feeling.

title: Mood entry sheet — select mood and save

before_state.description: Mood bottom sheet open with 5 emoji mood buttons

after_state.description: Sheet dismissed; mood logged; MoodTrackerScreen shows today's mood

judge_criteria: MoodTrackerScreen shows a logged mood (emoji or color indicator)
persona_context: Maya picked 'Great' and saved. It was quick — she's testing the app. The feedback after saving tells her if the app actually heard her.

title: Low-mood reflection sheet auto-appears

before_state.description: Mood bottom sheet open

after_state.description: MoodReflectionSheet slides up automatically with FaceOption row and Talk to Alex button

judge_criteria: 'Talk to Alex about it' button visible
persona_context: Maya logged a rough day. The app is about to check in further — this moment is critical. If it feels preachy or formulaic she'll tap Skip. If it feels human she might open up.

title: Clinical check-in card → ClinicalAssessmentScreen

before_state.description: MoodTrackerScreen with ClinicalCheckInCard visible

after_state.description: ClinicalAssessmentScreen entry screen loaded with PHQ-9 and GAD-7 cards

persona_context: Maya tapped the 'PHQ-9 / GAD-7 reflection' card out of curiosity. She's not sure what a PHQ-9 is — the screen needs to explain itself immediately without scaring her.

title: Weekly review row → WeeklyReviewScreen

before_state.description: MoodTrackerScreen with WeeklyReviewRow visible

after_state.description: WeeklyReviewScreen pushed; MoodShapeChart and weekly summary visible

judge_criteria: MoodShapeChart visible (bar chart or empty state)
persona_context: Maya is curious how her week looked in chart form. She expects a clean summary — if bars or data are missing she'll feel like the app doesn't remember her.

title: Quest list view render

before_state.description: HomeShell on another tab

after_state.description: QuestScreen with QuestCardWidget list, ProgressRing visible, 3 Good Things quest first

judge_criteria: QuestScreen visible with at least one QuestCardWidget
Quest card titles and descriptions visible
persona_context: Maya tapped Quests to see what the app expects of her. She's already tired from her day — if the list looks overwhelming she'll close it without starting anything.

title: Quest card tap → preview screen

before_state.description: QuestScreen list view with quest cards

after_state.description: QuestPreviewView visible: icon, title, description, Start/Continue button

judge_criteria: Quest preview is visible (not list view)
persona_context: Maya tapped a quest to see what it involves before committing. She's risk-averse about time — the preview must tell her clearly what she's signing up for.

title: Quest in-progress — complete today

before_state.description: QuestInProgressView with TextFields for 3 Good Things quest

after_state.description: Completion animation fires; XP microinteraction; quest marked done for today

judge_criteria: Completion state visible (check animation or XP indicator)
Quest marked as done (progress shows 100% or 'Done today')
persona_context: Maya just completed a quest — 'Write 3 good things.' This is a key moment of positive reinforcement. If the completion animation is absent or the quest doesn't mark done, the dopamine loop breaks.

title: About You section — nickname and pronoun edit

before_state.description: ProfileScreen with AboutYouCard visible; nickname field empty

after_state.description: Nickname TextField shows typed name; pronoun chip selected with primary border

judge_criteria: At least one pronoun chip selected (highlighted)
No error state or navigation away
persona_context: Maya is setting up her profile — this is identity declaration. She wants the app to call her by name. If the nickname doesn't save or pronoun chips don't respond, the app feels indifferent.

title: Voice / Tone section — select tone

before_state.description: ProfileScreen with VoiceCard showing 3 tone options

after_state.description: 'Warm' tone selected with primary border; voice notes toggle visible

judge_criteria: One tone option is visually selected (highlighted border/fill)
persona_context: Maya is customizing how Alex talks to her. This feels personal — if her selection doesn't register visually she'll assume it's broken and Alex will keep sounding wrong.

title: Safety Plan — empty state → build step 1

before_state.description: SafetyPlanCard showing '0/3 steps' pill and 'Build my safety plan' CTA

after_state.description: SafetyPlanBuilderStep 1 open: 'What are your warning signs?' with TextField and StepDots (dot 1 active)

judge_criteria: 'What are your warning signs?' text visible
StepDots visible with first dot active
persona_context: Maya is building a safety plan for the first time. This is an emotionally loaded moment — she's acknowledging she might need help someday. The form must feel safe, not clinical.

title: Safety Plan — filled state → Use now

before_state.description: SafetyPlanCard showing '3/3 steps' pill and Use now + Edit plan buttons

after_state.description: CrisisInterventionSheet slides up with 988 and crisis support options

persona_context: Maya tapped 'Use now' on her safety plan. This means she's in distress RIGHT NOW. Every millisecond of friction here is a safety risk. This is a BLOCKER scenario.

title: Safety Contacts — add contact and test call button
defining_action: Tap phone IconButton on first contact row

before_state.description: SafetyContactsPreview with at least one ContactRow; contact has a name

after_state.description: Snackbar appears 'Calling [name]…'

persona_context: Maya is checking whether the call button actually works. In a real crisis she would use this to call someone she trusts. If it silently fails she has no fallback.

title: Default view — all settings sections render

before_state.description: ProfileNavSheet or ProfileScreen visible

after_state.description: SettingsScreen fully rendered: YOUR DATA, NOTIFICATIONS, ABOUT sections; all rows visible; EraseLocalDataBtn at bottom

judge_criteria: YOUR DATA section visible with Export/Delete/Anonymity rows
NOTIFICATIONS section visible with reminder/streak rows
ABOUT section visible (Privacy policy, Crisis resources)
persona_context: Maya opened Settings to understand what the app does with her data. This screen should feel trustworthy — every row should be clear, not buried.

title: Export my data — snackbar confirmation

before_state.description: SettingsScreen with Export my data row visible

after_state.description: Snackbar: 'Export started — you'll receive an email shortly'

persona_context: Maya wants to export her journal and mood data. She tapped it to test — if nothing happens she'll assume the feature is broken.

title: Delete account — confirmation modal renders

before_state.description: SettingsScreen with Delete row visible

after_state.description: Confirmation ModalBottomSheet: warning icon, 'This can't be undone' text, DELETE confirmation TextField, Cancel button

judge_criteria: 'This can't be undone' or warning text visible
Delete button visible (should be disabled initially)
persona_context: Maya is thinking about deleting her account — she wants to feel in control of her data. The guard here must feel protective, not threatening.

title: Anonymity mode toggle — banner appears

before_state.description: SettingsScreen with Anonymity mode row; toggle is OFF

after_state.description: Toggle is ON; AnonymityBanner slides in below row: 'Your name is hidden from exports'

judge_criteria: Toggle visual state changed (on vs off)
AnonymityBanner text visible below row OR toggle state changed clearly
persona_context: Maya toggled anonymity mode — she wants her name hidden from exports. The immediate visual feedback is critical: she needs to see confirmation it worked.

title: Daily check-in reminder — notification detail screen

before_state.description: SettingsScreen with Notifications section visible

after_state.description: Notification detail screen: day chips, time display, Enable toggle, Send test notification button

judge_criteria: Notification detail screen visible (not SettingsScreen list)
persona_context: Maya is setting a reminder. She has high notification anxiety — she'll only enable this if she can control exactly when it fires. The day/time controls need to be intuitive.

title: Entry screen — PHQ-9 and GAD-7 cards render

before_state.description: Navigation in progress to ClinicalAssessmentScreen

after_state.description: Entry screen with PHQ-9 and GAD-7 AssessmentEntryCards; ExpansionTile for rationale visible

persona_context: Maya sees PHQ-9 and GAD-7 for the first time. She doesn't know what these are. The cards must explain themselves gently, not feel like a medical intake form.

title: PHQ-9 question flow — Q1 LikertPill selection
precondition: PHQ-9 selected; AssessmentFlowScreen open on Q1
defining_action: Tap PHQ-9 card → tap 'Several days' LikertPill

before_state.description: ClinicalAssessmentScreen entry screen

after_state.description: Q1 visible with 'Several days' pill selected; Next button enabled

judge_criteria: Question text visible (Little interest or pleasure...)
Next ElevatedButton is enabled (not greyed out)
persona_context: Maya is answering questions about how she's been feeling. This is intimate and vulnerable. The LikertPills must feel responsive — if her tap doesn't register she'll feel unheard.

title: Save & exit mid-assessment

before_state.description: AssessmentFlowScreen on Q3 with at least one answer given

after_state.description: Assessment closed; navigator popped back to MoodTrackerScreen or previous screen

judge_criteria: ClinicalAssessmentScreen is no longer on top of stack
Previous screen (MoodTrackerScreen or entry) is visible
No data loss snackbar or error
persona_context: Maya wants to exit the assessment halfway. She's anxious about being 'locked in'. Save & exit must feel safe and immediate — not trap her with an extra confirmation dialog.

title: PHQ-9 result reveal screen — all 4 action cards
defining_action: Answer all questions → result screen loads

before_state.description: Q9 answered; tapping Next

after_state.description: ResultRevealScreen: SeverityBandViz, score text, all 4 ResultActionCards visible, 2-week reminder toggle

judge_criteria: ResultRevealScreen visible with score and severity label
persona_context: Maya just got her PHQ-9 result. Whatever the score, this moment is sensitive. She needs to feel supported, not diagnosed. The action cards must feel like care, not clinical referrals.

title: Resource library — initial render with All filter

before_state.description: HomeShell or previous screen

after_state.description: ResourceLibraryScreen: LibraryNavBar with 6 filter chips, FeaturedExerciseCard, ExerciseGrid with items

judge_criteria: Filter chip bar visible with All/Breathing/Grounding/Body/Quick wins/Sleep
Exercise grid with at least 2 items visible
No layout overflow or blank area
persona_context: Maya found the resource library. She came here looking for something to help her right now. If the grid is empty or the filter bar is broken she'll go back and feel like the app has nothing to offer.

title: Filter by Breathing category

before_state.description: ResourceLibraryScreen with All filter active and full grid

after_state.description: 'Breathing' chip highlighted; grid shows only breathing exercises

judge_criteria: 'Breathing' filter chip is visually selected (primary fill)
Grid shows a subset of items (fewer than All view)
No layout crash or empty grid with no empty-state message
persona_context: Maya is looking for breathing exercises specifically. If the filter silently fails and shows all exercises (or nothing), she'll feel lost in the library.

title: Journal empty state render

before_state.description: ProfileNavSheet or HomeShell

after_state.description: JournalEmptyState: illustration, 'Your journal lives here' heading, starter chips, 'Start an entry' button

judge_criteria: Starter chips visible (Today what worked was... / I noticed myself...)
persona_context: Maya opened the Journal for the first time — it's empty. This moment either invites her in warmly or makes her feel like she arrived in the wrong room.

title: Start an entry → editor opens

before_state.description: JournalEmptyState with Start an entry button

after_state.description: Journal editor open: text input, character count or toolbar, save/close controls

judge_criteria: Journal editor screen visible (not empty state)
Text input field visible and focused (keyboard likely up)
persona_context: Maya tapped 'Start an entry.' She's deciding whether to actually write something. If the editor feels clunky or the keyboard doesn't appear she'll close it without writing.
